source_title: GitHub pull request disruption on 13 November
evidence_description: The feed records GitHub opening the incident at 15:47 UTC on 13 November 2026 and reporting it resolved at 18:29 UTC. The current resolution update was last modified at 21:45 UTC on 23 November, ten days after its creation. That later text reports a 13 November merge-timeout event and attributes it, together with a 16 November event, to storage read-bandwidth saturation and a disk-configuration setting. It reports mitigation by changing the setting and moving load.
investigation_relevance: The later explanation must not be presented as text published on 13 November. The feed does not preserve the earlier wording of that update. The cause and metrics are GitHub's account, not independently verified; no connection to Microsoft or aviation incidents is established.

source_title: GitHub pull request disruption on 16 November
evidence_description: The feed records GitHub opening the incident at 11:59 UTC on 16 November 2026. Its reports describe elevated pull-request merge timeouts and later workflow delays, followed by monitoring and an operator-reported resolution at 16:26 UTC. The present resolution update was last modified on 20 November at 18:50 UTC. The later account reports an average 2.9 percent merge timeout rate, a peak of 7.1 percent, and the storage-bandwidth and disk-configuration explanation for both the 13 and 16 November events.
investigation_relevance: The November 20 account is a later revision; the original resolved text is not in this saved feed. It is the same provider account appearing in EV-0049, not independent corroboration. Actual customer outcomes and a connection to other case incidents are not established.

source_title: GitHub Copilot model availability on 13 November
evidence_description: At 20:14 UTC on 13 November 2026 GitHub reported degraded availability of specified models in Copilot and attributed it to an upstream model-provider issue, advising use of another model or automatic selection. An update reported the incident resolved at 21:27 UTC; its present text was last modified at 21:38 UTC and says availability improved after the upstream provider mitigated the issue.
investigation_relevance: This is GitHub's account of a service dependency and mitigation; the feed does not identify the upstream provider or independently verify cause or individual outcomes. It does not establish a compromise or a connection to the other incidents.

source_title: How Phishing Campaigns Exploited the Microsoft 365 Outage
evidence_description: Trellix researchers report observing 252 outage-themed emails across more than 30 organisations between approximately 17:04 and 20:38 Coordinated Universal Time on 13 November. The reported messages used service-health and held-message lures. Trellix describes a multi-stage route ending in a Microsoft-like sign-in page and discusses the risk of captured sessions.
investigation_relevance: The count is limited to Trellix observations, not a worldwide count. Trellix reports the same three sender domains and an intermediary destination described by Microsoft in EV-0021. That overlap supports a relationship between source reports, not proof of independent samples, a named operator, successful account compromise, or a cause of the outage. Trellix says its suggested link to a particular phishing kit is unconfirmed.

source_title: Flash Alert: Weaponizing the November 2026 Microsoft Outage
evidence_description: Cofense researcher Jacob Malimban reports an outage-themed email that impersonated a Microsoft service notification and led to a Microsoft-like sign-in page. Cofense describes the first credential submission being rejected and a second submission redirecting to Microsoft.
investigation_relevance: The page describes how the phishing page behaved; it does not establish that any identified victim submitted working credentials, that credentials were captured, or that an account was compromised. The report shares an intermediary domain with the Microsoft and Trellix reports, which does not independently establish one operator or independent events. Its suggestion of generative artificial intelligence is not established evidence.

source_title: The Microsoft Outage Brought a Surge of Phishing Email
evidence_description: KnowBe4 reports that its product telemetry detected outage-themed phishing on 13 November at approximately 468 times its 9–11 November daily detection average; user reports were approximately 187 times that baseline. It describes four example lures, including held messages, a security check, an Exchange notice and a Teams-style message.
investigation_relevance: The ratios are KnowBe4's reported product-telemetry comparisons against a three-day baseline, not counts of attacks worldwide or evidence of successful compromises. Absolute counts and sample overlap with other vendors are not established by this record. The company separately relies on a preliminary Microsoft report for technical outage context.

source_authority: Australian Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
source_title: 235-2026: Services Restored: Thursday 05 November 2026 – COLS & COLSB2G
evidence_description: Before the later 13, 15 and 23 November notices already in the case, the department reported that a disruption affected cargo lodgements as of approximately 09:12 Australian Eastern Daylight Time on 4 November. Its notice reported restoration at 11:45 on 5 November. The department said importers and brokers may have faced delays receiving biosecurity assessment outcomes and staff used workarounds when lodgement reference number issues were identified.
investigation_relevance: The actual start time, number of affected lodgements, clearance or shipping delay outcomes, common cause with later incidents, and whether every workaround succeeded are not established by this notice.

source_title: Global Microsoft outage
evidence_description: The council reported that by 11:30 on 13 November it had paused online payments and applications as a precaution, with in-person payments still available. On 14 November it said those services would remain paused over the weekend even if Microsoft's services returned. At 10:30 on 16 November it reported queued submissions and attachments were being processed, and by its 14:00 update said online payments and applications were operating normally.
investigation_relevance: The updates do not give the exact time each service resumed, the number of affected residents, completion of the queued submissions, the accessibility of in-person alternatives to each resident, or independent technical causation. Times are the council's local times.

source_title: Notice extending two request-for-quotation closing dates
evidence_description: The museum's 16 November notice says a Microsoft system outage or technical challenge on 13 November affected its closing process. It extends the closing dates for two requests for quotations from 13 November to noon on 17 November 2026.

source_title: Cofense report of email-security control bypass
evidence_description: Cofense reported that the outage-themed campaign bypassed Abnormal Security, Mimecast and Microsoft ATP. This records the company’s reported observation; it is not independent verification.
investigation_relevance: This records a control-related claim omitted from EV-0053. The source does not establish configurations or the exact message timing, independently explain why controls missed a message, or prove that an outage caused bypass or that a user account was compromised. Microsoft EV-0021 separately reported blocking and quarantine; no same-sample comparison establishes a contradiction.

source_title: Anthropic Microsoft 365 connector and Claude for Outlook
evidence_description: Anthropic reported mail, calendar and search failures for many connector and Claude for Outlook requests during an impact interval from 12 November 16:03 UTC to 13 November 16:40 UTC. On 12 November at 22:23 UTC it explicitly attributed the issue to a Microsoft 365 incident. At 15:40 UTC on 13 November it described signs of recovery while some search requests still errored. At 21:49 UTC it marked its incident resolved while saying Microsoft was still completing recovery and occasional errors or delays could remain.
investigation_relevance: This is Anthropic’s attribution and impact interval. It does not establish the underlying Microsoft root cause, impact on every customer, completed backlogs or a connection to other unrelated incidents. UTC; capture occurred 26 November. The 21:49 status update was posted later than the stated 16:40 impact end; do not collapse the milestones.

source_title: OpenAI Microsoft 365 connector
evidence_description: OpenAI published an investigation notice on 12 November at 18:29 UTC stating new Microsoft connector connections might be broken and tools might not work as expected. At 16:20 UTC on 13 November it reported signs of recovery and continued monitoring. It posted an operator-reported resolution at 00:18 UTC on 14 November.
investigation_relevance: OpenAI’s captured notice does not explicitly establish that this connector incident had the same technical cause as Anthropic’s or the broader Microsoft incident. Temporal overlap and the product name alone are not proof. The page does not establish individual customer recovery. UTC values were verified in embedded timestamps in the preserved OpenAI HTML; its web display can vary by reader timezone.

source_title: OpenAI Codex GitHub review and merge failures
evidence_description: At 16:27 UTC on 25 November OpenAI reported that some Codex users might miss automated GitHub pull-request reviews or encounter merge errors; it attributed those failures to a GitHub service disruption. At 16:58 UTC it said GitHub had reported a mitigation and OpenAI was monitoring Codex review and merge operations. The saved page still described monitoring when retrieved on 26 November at 03:18 UTC.
investigation_relevance: This is OpenAI’s attribution and describes some users, not proof of impact on every user. The page does not identify a specific GitHub incident ID, independent root cause, or individual outcomes. Monitoring is not proof of recovery or continuing failure beyond capture. UTC values were verified in the preserved OpenAI HTML; event times do not use browser-local display.

source_title: GitHub cross-product disruption on 25 November
evidence_description: GitHub reported degraded experiences across multiple products beginning at 15:55 UTC on 25 November. It marked the incident resolved at 16:52 UTC and said a detailed root-cause analysis would be shared when available.
investigation_relevance: The saved page supports GitHub’s reported milestones and affected services, not independent proof of the cause or customer outcomes. OpenAI attributed its Codex failures to a GitHub disruption without naming this particular GitHub incident; the linkage to this specific record remains an inference pending confirmation. UTC; the GitHub resolution notice preceded OpenAI’s 16:58 UTC monitoring notice. Those statements are distinct milestones, not a measured period of downstream failure.
